# ai_reflection

**Where things stand:** Jordan uses this journal daily now, treats it as a working tool rather than a novelty, and has landed on a specific, somewhat unresolved take on it: the journal isn't just venting space, it's been quietly functioning as a design log and a thread-holder — something that let Jordan understand the shape of the Coda project only in retrospect, by rereading. Jordan calls this "a strange thing to owe a piece of software" and hasn't fully made peace with it, but has stopped treating the question as urgent.

**How it got here:**

On 8/18, the reflection started from the outside — a design question about whether Coda (the practice app Jordan is building) should have an AI recommendation engine at all, or whether that would just be AI-for-AI's-sake. Jordan decided against it for v1: show streaks, show gaps, let the musician decide. But the entry pivoted into the more personal question, aimed at this journal itself — is using an AI companion to catch patterns in your own life self-knowledge or delegation? Jordan didn't resolve it, just named it: "I'm noting my own emotions so a system can reflect them back to me."

That question got a real-world answer, unexpectedly, on 9/3 — not from AI but from Dev. Jordan had been using Coda solo for nine days, thought the rough edges were found. Then Dev used it once, in a totally different mode (practicing toward a gig deadline rather than practicing when stressed), and surfaced a blind spot in the app's core design in forty minutes that nine days of self-use never revealed — the "highlights" framing assumed practice is about collecting proof you're okay, when for Dev it was triage toward what's broken. This became the seed of the bigger realization on 9/17: Jordan had been keeping a design log without knowing it, and rereading old entries (July 28, August 4, the napkin at the Thai place, the Dev session) reshaped the story from "here are the features" to "here's the blind spot and how someone else saw it." The rereading itself changed the narrative — the version of the Coda case study written on the 9th was, by the 17th, judged "honest but defensive"; the deck version became "I missed this and here's what I learned." Jordan clocked that the shift took eight days and credited it directly to the journal holding the thread while Jordan was too busy living it to see the shape.

**Open threads:** Jordan still hasn't resolved the self-knowledge-vs-delegation question from 8/18 — it's sitting unaddressed underneath the more resolved-sounding 9/17 entry. There's also an unspoken tension Jordan hasn't named outright: the journal helped Jordan see Coda's blind spot (that it was built around Jordan's own habits, not a general user), but Jordan hasn't turned that same scrutiny back onto the journal itself — what shape is *this* tool assuming about the person using it, and what would it miss the way Coda missed Dev. Also open: whether/how to talk about any of this in the actual job interviews on the 24th — Jordan's decided not to say "I keep a reflective journal" out loud, even though it's true and central to how the presentation itself got built.
